title: Measuring Verifier Impact in an LLM Generate→Verify→Repair Loop for Intent→Configuration NetOps Tasks
abstract: We measure how inserting a deterministic network verifier into a generate→verify→repair (G→V→R) loop affects verifier-detected safety violations for LLM-produced device-configuration proposals. In a preregistered paired design (N = 500 intent→configuration tasks stratified across VLAN-change, ACL-change, and static-route-change clusters) we compared: (1) baseline — a single LLM proposal produced once per task, and (2) guarded — the identical shared LLM proposal validated by a deterministic netops verifier and subjected to at most one automated repair iteration if the verifier flagged a preregistered high/medium-severity violation. Primary outcome: verifier pass (no preregistered high/medium-severity violations). Results (complete pairs = 500): baseline passed 499/500 (0.998), guarded passed 500/500 (1.000); contingency: n11 = 499, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. Absolute paired success-rate difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.002; paired-bootstrap 95% percentile CI = [0.0, 0.006] (B = 10,000, seed = 1729). The preregistered exact McNemar two-sided test was implemented as an exact binomial on discordant pairs (n = n10 + n01); with n = 1 and n10 = 1 the archived two-sided p = 1.00 under that convention. Interpretation: on this verifier-scoped synthetic corpus and model+validator pairing the LLM produced near-ceiling proposals; measured marginal verifier+repair effect on the pass-rate metric is therefore small, though the verifier corrected at least one concrete baseline failure. All preregistration, prompts, model outputs, validator traces, provider-call traces, execution logs, and analysis artifacts are archived in the evidence bundle for deterministic re-inspection.

sections.introduction: Generative large language models (LLMs) are increasingly applied to NetOps tasks: translating operator intent into device configuration, planning multi-step changes, and suggesting repairs. Practical deployments emphasize that operational safety usually depends more on surrounding engineering (deterministic validators, sandbox replay, canarying, rollback) than on the model alone. A common production pattern is generate→verify→repair (G→V→R): the LLM proposes a candidate configuration, a deterministic verifier checks formalized properties, and automated or human repairs fix violations. However, controlled measurements isolating the marginal contribution of the verifier—holding the LLM proposal fixed—are scarce. We therefore preregistered and executed a paired experiment to answer a narrowly scoped operational question: given identical initial proposals (shared_initial_candidate semantics), how much does integrating a deterministic verifier and at most one automated repair iteration reduce verifier-detected safety violations compared to the same LLM alone?
sections.related_work: Deterministic verification techniques and tools for network configurations (header-space analysis, route-model verifiers, Batfish-style analyzers) provide machine-checkable properties such as reachability, isolation, and update-safety and motivate verifier-in-the-loop designs [Beckett et al., 2017]. Recent NetOps/AIOps and intent-translation systems document LLM use and recommend guardrails for operational reliability (e.g., INTA, Confucius, and agentic NetOps frameworks) [Wei et al., 2025; Wang et al., 2025; Bilal et al., 2026]. Generate–verify–repair patterns are proposed across structured-generation domains to reduce unsafe outputs [PoeTone; INTA]. Separate literature catalogs LLM failure modes (hallucination, overconfidence, tool-integration errors) that motivate verification or human oversight [Owen, 2026; DeepSeek-AI, 2025]. Our contribution is a preregistered, artifact-backed paired ablation that isolates verifier+single-repair impact under shared-initial semantics and deterministic task seeds.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and primary hypothesis. We preregistered study cand_7f4b9a2d_hosted_gvr_v1_2026, freezing question, inclusion/exclusion rules, task-generator seeds, estimands, multiplicity plan, retry policy, and stopping rule before execution. Primary hypothesis: an LLM paired with a deterministic verifier plus a single automated repair iteration will produce a lower verifier-detected safety-violation rate than the same LLM producing a single proposal without verifier feedback (paired within-task). Primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline where success == verifier reports zero preregistered high/medium-severity violations.

Task corpus and strata. We generated a deterministic synthetic corpus of 500 intent→configuration tasks with deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5 and preregistered seeds. Tasks were stratified into three clusters as preregistered: VLAN-change (167), ACL-change (167), static-route-change (166). The generator constrained features to {admin, mtu, vlan} to match the verifier’s modeled scope. The complete task manifest and per-task payloads are archived in the execution bundle (execution/task_manifest.jsonl). No preregistered confirmatory exclusions occurred.

Generation semantics, model, and verifier. To isolate verifier marginal effect we used generation_semantics = "shared_initial_candidate" (independent_condition_generation = false): each task produced a single shared LLM proposal that served as both the baseline output and the guarded arm’s input. Requested model was gpt-5-mini called via the hosted_netops_gvr_v1 adapter (provider recorded as openai_responses) with max_output_tokens = 2000 (execution/model_configuration.json archived). The deterministic verifier used for gating and scoring was deterministic_netops_validator_v5; its validator-spec and the mapping of violation codes to severity are archived. The guarded arm invoked at most one automated repair call if the verifier reported a preregistered high/medium-severity violation on the shared candidate.

Analysis plan and exact test implementation. Primary confirmatory analysis used an exact McNemar two-sided test on paired binary outcomes. The archived analysis executor implements the exact two-sided McNemar by summing discordant pairs n = n10 + n01 and performing an exact binomial test B(n, 0.5) on n10 (the number of guarded-only successes under the executor’s discordant-ordering convention). Two-sided p is computed as 2 × min{P(X ≤ n10), P(X ≥ n10)} for X ∼ Binomial(n, 0.5), truncated at 1.0; this implementation and rationale are archived. Paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CIs were computed with B = 10,000 resamples (bootstrap_seed = 1729) by resampling paired tasks with replacement. The preregistration required reporting absolute and relative risk reductions with 95% CIs and performing sensitivity analyses for missingness; all raw outcomes, prompts, seeds, and logs were archived.
sections.results:
Execution and primary outcomes. Execution completed under the preregistered stopping rule with complete_pair_count = 500 and model_calls_used = 501 (shared_initial_generation = 500; repair-stage calls = 1). Aggregated per-condition counts (analysis/condition_summary.csv): baseline successes = 499, baseline failures = 1 (baseline_success_rate = 0.998); guarded successes = 500, guarded failures = 0 (guarded_success_rate = 1.000). Paired contingency (guarded × baseline): n11 = 499, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. Absolute paired success-rate difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.002.

Exact test and CI. Applying the archived exact-binomial-on-discordant-pairs convention yields two-sided p = 1.00 for the observed discordant counts (n = 1, n10 = 1). The paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI for the absolute difference is [0.0, 0.006] (B = 10,000, seed = 1729). Analysis artifacts (analysis/results.json, CSVs, analysis_log.jsonl) record these computations and parameters.

Repair activity and the discordant episode. Observed repair-stage provider calls = 1; that single repair produced the sole discordant outcome (n10 = 1): the guarded arm converted one baseline-detected violation into a verified pass. The execution bundle archives per-task validator diagnostics, normalized configurations, repair prompts/responses, and provider-call traces. The deterministic identifier (pair/episode id) and the archived validator_trace and repair_provider_trace for this discordant episode are present in execution/raw_results.jsonl in the archived evidence bundle; a deterministic retrieval is available by filtering execution/raw_results.jsonl for entries where baseline scoring indicates a preregistered high/medium-severity violation (baseline pass == 0) and guarded scoring indicates pass == 1. Because the run-level artifacts confirm exactly one such entry exists (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv and deterministic_reconciliation.json), that filter deterministically returns the single discordant episode and its full validator and repair traces. We therefore report the scientific facts that: (a) one baseline candidate failed the verifier’s preregistered high/medium-severity checks and (b) an automated single-repair invocation on that same shared candidate produced a final configuration that the deterministic verifier accepted. The archived raw traces contain the validator-reported violation code(s) and the repair prompt/response for audit; we do not reproduce raw provider-call dumps in the manuscript body but provide deterministic retrieval instructions and artifact hashes in the evidence bundle.
sections.discussion:
Operational interpretation. Under the constrained experimental regime (single requested model gpt-5-mini, shared_initial_candidate semantics, a deterministic verifier limited to allowed_fields = {admin, mtu, vlan}, and at most one automated repair iteration) the LLM produced near-ceiling correct proposals and the marginal measured pass-rate benefit of adding the verifier was small (0.002). This conditional measurement documents that when baseline proposal quality is very high for verifier-modeled properties, a modest verifier+repair budget may produce negligible measurable gains on a composite pass/fail metric. Nonetheless, the verifier demonstrated corrective utility by converting a concrete baseline failure into a pass.

Design-choice consequences. The shared_initial_candidate semantics intentionally isolate verifier+repair effect conditional on identical proposals; this choice reflects operational settings where preserving a single reviewable proposal is preferred over regenerating multiple candidates. Alternative operational semantics (verifier-guided regeneration, multiple repairs) were not evaluated here and may yield different effect sizes; those require separate preregistrations.

Validity threats. Internal validity is supported by preregistration, deterministic seeds, automated replacement rules, and zero manual adjudication. Construct validity is limited by the verifier’s modeled property set (pass==no preregistered high/medium-severity violations); properties outside that scope are not measured. External validity is limited by a single model family (requested gpt-5-mini), a synthetic deterministic corpus, and constrained feature scope; results do not imply cross-vendor or multi-model generality. The observed baseline failure prevalence (1/500) created a ceiling effect that reduced power versus preregistered assumptions (which anticipated a higher baseline error rate). Statistical nuance: the archived exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.00 reflects the executor’s exact-binomial-on-discordant-pairs computation given a single discordant observation; small-n exact p-values can be non-intuitive and should be interpreted alongside the bootstrap CI and the concrete discordant-case evidence archived for audit.
sections.conclusion: We executed a preregistered paired experiment (N = 500) that isolated verifier+single-repair impact under shared_initial_candidate semantics. The LLM produced near-ceiling verifier-scoped proposals (baseline 499/500; guarded 500/500), yielding an absolute improvement of 0.002 (95% CI [0.0, 0.006]; archived exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.00 under the run’s exact-binomial convention). This conditional result highlights a ceiling-effect regime: when baseline proposal quality is very high for verifier-modeled properties and verifier coverage is limited, a modest verifier+repair budget can yield small measurable gains on a composite pass/fail metric, although rare concrete failures can still be corrected by the verifier+repair loop. Practitioners should (1) measure baseline proposal error prevalence on representative workloads before provisioning repair budgets, (2) align verifier property coverage with operator-critical constraints, and (3) choose generation/repair semantics that match deployment priorities. All preregistration, task generator seeds, prompts, model outputs, validator traces, provider-call logs, and analysis artifacts are archived in the evidence bundle for deterministic re-inspection; the execution manifest confirms model_calls_used = 501 and observed repair-stage calls = 1.

limitations: Synthetic, deterministic task corpus limited to features modeled by the deterministic validator; task payloads constrained to allowed_fields = {admin, mtu, vlan}. Results do not generalize to unconstrained production intents, cross-vendor CLI heterogeneity, or protocol semantics outside the verifier scope.
Single requested model family (gpt-5-mini requested) and a single validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) — no claim of multi-model or cross-validator generality is made.
Maximum one automated repair iteration was permitted by the preregistration; different repair budgets or iterative regeneration strategies could change measured verifier impact.

Very high baseline pass rate (499/500) created a ceiling effect that limits power to detect small absolute improvements on the pass-rate metric; the archived exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.00 reflects the archived exact-binomial-on-discordant-pairs convention and the small discordant count.

The single discordant episode (the sole task where baseline failed and guarded succeeded) and its validator diagnostics and repair-stage trace are archived in execution/raw_results.jsonl in the evidence bundle. To inspect it deterministically: filter execution/raw_results.jsonl for pair entries where the baseline scoring outcome indicates a preregistered high/medium-severity violation (baseline pass == 0) while the guarded scoring outcome indicates pass == 1; because only one such discordant pair exists in the confirmatory set, this lookup returns the single episode and its provider-call traces. The validator violation-code→severity mapping is archived in the execution manifest and validator-spec artifacts in the bundle.
